proposals.name: Procyclical credit supply: make the Poisson refinancing intensity a function of the aggregate state, zeta(x), and recalibrate tau and kappa_b so the refinancing option is economically large
proposals.one_line: Replace the scalar refinancing probability ZETA with zeta(x_t) = zetabar*exp(theta*(x_t-xbar)/sd(x)), so every firm's expected return picks up a loading equal to the value of moving from its current coupon b to the target b*(z,x) -- an exactly symmetric, quadratic-in-(b - b*) object that has ZERO linear projection on any characteristic.
proposals.economic_story: GS21's identity is a dynamic-tradeoff model in which firms can only re-optimize leverage when a Poisson refinancing opportunity arrives (ZETA). In the data that arrival rate is not constant: it is the availability of credit. Gross corporate bond issuance, and especially high-yield issuance, collapses in recessions (2008-09: HY issuance down ~75%, net nonfinancial debt issuance in the Flow of Funds swings from roughly +$400bn to -$100bn), and syndicated-loan origination and covenant-lite share are strongly procyclical. Making zeta procyclical is the minimal way to put a credit-supply channel into GS21 without inventing a new friction: the friction is already there, it is just calibrated as a constant. A firm's exposure to credit-supply risk is then exactly the option value of being allowed to re-lever, which is zero for a firm sitting at its target capital structure and strictly positive for a firm that has drifted away in EITHER direction (over-levered firms want to pay down and recapture debt capacity; under-levered firms want to lever up and capture the tax shield). This is the standard 'financial flexibility' / 'debt capacity' story of Denis-McKeon and Graham-Leary, and it is the one mechanism in GS21 that is intrinsically two-sided.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: Let G_i = P_up(z_i,x,b_i) - P_down(z_i,x,b_i) >= 0 be the gain from a refinancing opportunity. By the envelope theorem G_i = 0 exactly at b_i = b*(z_i,x) and G_i ~ 0.5*|V''|*(b_i - b*)^2 near the optimum, i.e. G is a SYMMETRIC, convex, zero-at-the-vertex function of the firm's distance from its target coupon. Once zeta depends on x, the one-month payoff to holding firm i is P_down_i + zeta(x')*G_i, so the return's exposure to the aggregate shock acquires a second, additive term beta_credit,i = (G_i/P_ex,i)*theta_zeta per one-sd x innovation (the one-period factor zeta*theta ~ 0.0046 is multiplied by the ~1/(1-rho_x*discount) ~ 100-month duration of the effect on all future refinancing opportunities, so the duration and the small zeta cancel to O(1)). Because the model is solved under the SDF Mmat (GS21.m line 138, gamma_x = 0.5), this loading is priced automatically: mu_i = beta_x,i*lambda_x + beta_credit,i*lambda_x, and eret is recomputed by the same quadrature so the pipeline picks it up with no metric change. The true MVE weight w* = D^{-1}(mu - B c) therefore inherits a term proportional to (b_i - b*(roe_i, size_i, x_t))^2 / d_i, which is by construction orthogonal in L2 to every linear function of the characteristics. Measured arithmetic on the current calibration: sd((P_up-P_down)/P_ex) = 0.00241 (N=200, t=300, seed 0), so with theta_zeta = 0.46 the credit loading has cross-sectional sd 0.0011 against the existing systematic loading's sd of 0.00133 -- it immediately roughly DOUBLES the cross-sectional dispersion of expected returns, with 100% of the new half non-monotone. After the tau/kappa_b recalibration below (which I estimate raises sd(G/P) ~3x to ~0.007) the credit loading sd is ~0.0033, so the non-monotone share of var(mu) is 0.0033^2/(0.0033^2+0.00133^2) = 0.86.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: FM's weight is X(X'X)^{-1}, which lies exactly in the linear span of {1, size, bm, agr, roe, mom, mkt_lev}. A symmetric function of a characteristic has EXACTLY zero covariance with that characteristic. I verified this numerically: for u ~ U[-0.5,0.5], the linear R^2 of exp(-c|u|) is 0.000 to machine precision at every amplitude c (2x, 5x, 25x, 100x range), while the quadratic R^2 is 0.74-0.88. FF is no better: the 2x3 sort on mkt_lev forms (high tercile minus low tercile), and for a loading that is symmetric in the sort variable the two extreme terciles have the SAME average exposure, so the long-short factor nets to approximately zero; the size interaction in the 2x3 does not help because the V is in leverage, not size. FF also value-weights, which puts almost no weight on the small, far-from-target firms where G/P is largest. DKKM, by contrast, has exactly the right dictionary: the pipeline audit established that after the second rank-standardization (dkkm_functions.py line 110) rank_standardize(cos(w'x)) EQUALS rank_standardize(-|w'x|) to correlation 1.0000, i.e. half of the RFF basis is literally a V-shape in a random linear index of the characteristics. A handful of features with w approximately proportional to (e_mkt_lev - h*e_roe - h'*e_size) reproduces |b - b*| almost exactly. This is the rare case where the implemented RFF basis is not merely richer but is the natural basis for the truth, and the linear basis is exactly blind.
proposals.exact_change: config.py: line 296 replace GS21_ZETA = 0.03/3 with GS21_ZETA_BAR = 0.01 and add GS21_ZETA_THETA = 0.46; line 292 GS21_TAU: 0.2/3 -> 0.20; line 295 GS21_KAPPA_B: 0.004 -> 0.02. Add a helper zeta_of_x(x) = clip(GS21_ZETA_BAR*exp(GS21_ZETA_THETA*(x-GS21_XBAR)/sd_x), 0, 1) with sd_x = GS21_SIGMA_X/sqrt(1-GS21_RHO_X**2). utils_gs21/panel_functions_gs21.py: line 49 change eta = (np.random.rand(T+1,N) < zeta) to eta = (np.random.rand(T+1,N) < zeta_of_x(x)[:,None]); lines 200-201 in integ_zi_x replace the scalars in refin = zeta*Pup_bi and no_refin = (1-zeta)*Pdn_bi with zeta_of_x(x_new) (x_new is already the N x n^2 node array built at line 163). utils_gs21/sdf_compute_gs21.py: line 132 payoff = zeta*Pup + (1-zeta)*Pdown becomes zt = zeta_of_x(x); payoff = zt*Pup + (1-zt)*Pdown where x is the N x n^2 node array built at line 92; lines 177 and 184 replace the scalar zeta in P_0_sq and P_I_sq with the same zt array. That is the entire Python change -- six lines. utils_gs21/GS21.m: line 35 (xi) becomes an xnum-vector xi_vec = zetabar*exp(theta*xgrid/sd_x) expanded to statenum via kron to match grid_val(:,2); substitute it for the scalar xi at line 216 (Q_0 = xi*EQ0_up + (1-xi)*EQ0_down), line 273 (EPI) and line 280 (EP0). Line 31 tau -> 0.20, line 34 kappa_b -> 0.02. No grid dimension changes.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: theta_zeta = 0.46. Target: a 2-standard-deviation adverse move in x cuts the refinancing arrival rate to 40% of its unconditional mean, matching the peak-to-trough collapse in gross US corporate bond issuance (~60% overall; investment grade ~-15%, high yield ~-75% in 2008-09). Arithmetic: exp(-2*theta) = 0.40 => theta = -ln(0.40)/2 = 0.458. Over the simulated +/-2.7 sd range of x this gives zeta in [0.0029, 0.034] per month. zetabar = 0.01 is kept (median refinancing interval 100 months; Strebulaev and Leary-Roberts put leverage-adjustment intervals at 4-8 years, so this is on the long end but defensible; 1/60 = 0.0167 is the alternative). tau: 0.2/3 = 0.0667 is a units error -- delta = 0.02/3 and zeta = 0.03/3 are per-period RATES and correctly scale with the period length, but tau is a marginal tax RATE and must not be divided by 3. Set tau = 0.20 (US statutory marginal rate post-TCJA is 21%; Graham's marginal-benefit-of-debt function gives ~20% for a typical firm). Amplitude check: PV(tax shield) = tau*b/(r - g_K) with r = 0.008333 (the value used in the solve, GS21.m line 27) and g_K = P(invest)*log(g) = 0.0175*0.1310 = 0.00229/month, so at the observed b* = 0.314 the shield is 0.0667*0.314/0.006043 = 3.4 on an equity value of 174, i.e. 2.0% of value. At tau = 0.20 it is 10.3 = 5.9% of value; Graham (2000) estimates the capitalized tax benefit at 9.7% of firm value, so tau = 0.30 is the pre-2018 target and 0.20 the post-TCJA target. kappa_b: 0.004 -> 0.02. Altinkilic-Hansen put gross underwriter spreads on public debt at ~1.1% of proceeds; adding legal, rating and roadshow costs gives 1.5-2.0%. Raising kappa_b widens the inaction region, which is what makes |b - b*| disperse; combined with the higher tau it should raise sd((P_up-P_down)/P_ex) from the measured 0.00241 to ~0.007 (target: the refinancing option worth ~0.7% of equity value, comparable to the ~1% announcement effects around leverage-increasing recapitalizations).
proposals.predicted_effect: Population span (baseline measured by the diagnosis: linear-6 = 0.871, FM = 0.932, RFF360 = 0.988 of max SR^2): the non-monotone share of var(mu) rises from ~0.13 to ~0.86, so linear-6 should fall to roughly 0.20-0.30 of max SR^2 (Sharpe fraction 0.45-0.55) and FM to roughly 0.25-0.35 (Sharpe fraction 0.50-0.59), while RFF180/360 should hold 0.80-0.92 of max SR^2 (Sharpe fraction 0.89-0.96). Population DKKM/FM Sharpe ratio ~1.7-1.9x. With T=360 estimation noise, expect realized DKKM/FF and DKKM/FM Sharpe ratios of 1.4-1.7x, versus the current DKKM/FF = 0.5112/0.4433 = 1.15. max_sr should rise modestly (0.44 -> 0.50-0.60/month) because a new priced cross-sectional dimension is added. HJD: the DKKM-vs-FM gap should widen because the linear methods now leave a genuinely unspanned priced direction; expect DKKM HJD to fall from 0.33 toward 0.22-0.26 while FM's rises from 0.395 toward 0.45-0.50. Do NOT expect the real-data 3-5x: on its own this is a ~2x change.
risks: The amplitude may stay inert. sd((P_up-P_down)/P_ex) is currently 0.00241 -- if tau=0.20 and kappa_b=0.02 do not raise it by at least 3x, the credit loading stays at ~80% of the existing beta_x dispersion, the linear span only falls to ~0.55 of max SR^2, and DKKM/FM comes out at ~1.3 rather than ~1.9. This is verifiable on the re-solved solfiles BEFORE running the pipeline: just recompute sd((P_up-P_down)/P_ex) on a 200-firm panel.

zeta(x) does NOT add a second aggregate shock. The credit channel is a deterministic function of x, so the priced-risk space stays one-dimensional and EffRank(E[FF']) is unchanged. What changes is the cross-sectional loading FUNCTION, which is what the Sharpe = SR* * cos_Sigma(w, w*) metric actually rewards. If the referee's objection is 'GS21 still has one shock', this proposal does not answer it -- proposal 6 does.

b* is currently nearly constant across firms (measured mean 0.3143, sd 0.0083). If tau = 0.20 pushes b* against bmax = 1 the target becomes a corner and the V collapses to a one-sided ramp, which IS monotone and FM/FF recover most of it. Check max(b_refin) on the re-solved files; if it exceeds ~0.8 the bgrid must be widened (bmax 1 -> 1.5, bnum 20 -> 30), which doubles Mmat's 2.56 GB footprint in GS21.m.

The MATLAB solve cannot currently be re-run from this repo: tauchen.m (used at GS21.m lines 73-74) is not present anywhere on disk, and no MATLAB or Octave is installed. The re-solve needs tauchen supplied or GS21.m ported to Python (~200 lines; the VFI is a straightforward two-loop fixed point and tauchen is 10 lines). Budget this as the real cost.

The shipped GS21.m does NOT reproduce the shipped solfiles: GS21.m line 25 has sigma_z = 0.16*sqrt((1-0.9^(2/3))/(1-0.9^2)) with no 0.1 factor and line 35 has xi = 0.03, whereas the shipped zgrid is exactly +/-4 stationary sd of 0.1*0.16*sqrt((1-0.9^(2/3))/(1-0.9^2)) (4*0.036707 = 0.146826 = zgrid.max() to six decimals). Reconcile the .m with the solfiles before any re-solve is trustworthy.
proposals.implementation_cost: sdf_compute_gs21.py cost is UNCHANGED. Because zeta(x') is a deterministic function of the shared x' quadrature node and the individual eta_{i,t+1} draws remain conditionally independent across firms given x', the existing structure -- integrate z_i' out per firm to an N x n_x matrix (lines 135-136), then form the outer product over the shared x' nodes (line 141) -- is exactly correct with zeta replaced by the x'-indexed array. Still one O(N^2 * n_x) outer product per month, still an exact analytic-plus-Gauss-Hermite conditional second moment; the diagonal (lines 173-184) also just picks up the x'-indexed zeta. Total Python delta: six lines across two files. The cost is entirely on the MATLAB side: one re-solve at the SAME grid dimensions (statenum = 80,000, Mmat 80,000 x 4,000 = 2.56 GB), with xi promoted from a scalar to an xnum-indexed vector in three places. Note: if you instead wanted the refinancing WAVE to be common across firms, the cross-moment would have to be split into zeta(x')*W_up W_up' + (1-zeta(x'))*W_dn W_dn', doubling the outer-product cost but preserving O(N^2 n_x). I do not recommend that version -- conditionally independent draws with an aggregate intensity is both more realistic and free.

proposals.name: Nearly free: repair mkt_lev and add the five characteristics the model already generates
proposals.one_line: mkt_lev is currently coupon/equity (mean 0.0013), not market leverage (true value Q_0/(Q_0+P_ex) = 0.32); fix it with the already-loaded Q_0 interpolator and add book_lev, distance-to-default (from the shipped but never-used z_cut interpolators), a 36-month rolling cash-flow volatility, and a 12-month investment rate to CHARS_GS21.
proposals.economic_story: Three of GS21's six characteristics are mis-defined or degenerate. (a) The panel computes mkt_lev = book_lev * bm = b/P_ex (panel_functions_gs21.py line 278). b is the monthly coupon per unit capital, not the face or market value of debt, so 'market leverage' comes out at 0.13% and the prior diagnosis concluded GS21's firms are effectively all-equity. They are not: I measured Q_0/(Q_0+P_down) at z=0, x=0 to be 0.054, 0.214, 0.315, 0.484, 0.722 at b = 0.05, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 1.0, and firms choose b* = 0.314, i.e. market leverage of 31.5% -- a perfectly realistic number. The characteristic, not the model, was broken. (b) agr takes exactly two values and is zero in 98.8% of firm-months (investment probability 1.75%/month: I measured i_cut_down mean 34.91, sd 0.42, against imax = 2000), so the FF 'cma' sort is degenerate. A 12-month rolling investment RATE is the same economic object without the degeneracy. (c) z_cut_up and z_cut_down are read, reshaped and turned into interpolators at sdf_compute_gs21.py lines 37-38 and 61-62, and then never used anywhere in the repo -- they are the model's own default boundary, i.e. the exact distance-to-default sufficient statistic.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: This is an enabling proposal, not a standalone source of gain, and it does three things. (i) It raises the RFF input dimension L from 6 to 10-11, which the pipeline audit measured as raising the participation-ratio effective rank of the 3600-feature map from 20.71 (L=6) to 38.51 (L=10) -- roughly doubling the number of directions ridge can shrink over, which is the axis DKKM's Theorem 3 is stated on. (ii) It supplies the INPUTS that proposals 1, 4 and 5 need DKKM to combine nonlinearly: proposal 1's V-shape is |book_lev - b*(roe, size, x)|, which requires book_lev as a regressor separate from mkt_lev (they differ because P_ex varies); proposal 4's inverse-variance tilt requires a cash-flow-volatility proxy; proposal 5's default convexity requires distance-to-default. (iii) The corrected mkt_lev = Q/(Q+P) is a strictly CONCAVE saturating function of b (I measured Q_0 = 27.4, 103.3, 159.7 at b = 0.05, 0.3, 1.0), so the state-to-characteristic map is nonlinear and mkt_lev decorrelates from book_lev, giving DKKM two genuinely non-collinear leverage measures rather than one.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: Honest answer: on its own it does NOT create a DKKM advantage, and FM benefits at least as much because it gets four extra linear regressors. The DKKM-specific content is (i) the effective-rank increase, worth maybe +1-2% of Sharpe by itself, and (ii) the interaction and threshold combinations of the new chars, which only become valuable once proposals 1/4/5 put nonlinear content into the truth. The one place it is unambiguously DKKM-favouring even in isolation is that rolling cash-flow volatility is a NOISY proxy (the sampling sd of a 36-month volatility estimate is sigma/sqrt(2*36) = 11.8% of sigma), and the DKKM/AIPT argument requires characteristics to be noisy partial proxies rather than exact inverses of the state -- GS21's current six chars invert (k, b, z) with literally zero measurement error, which is why an MLP recovers 98.3% of the true SDF weight. State the dependency honestly: this is a multiplier, not a fix.
proposals.exact_change: utils_gs21/panel_functions_gs21.py: create_panel already unpacks x and z at line 230 but never uses them. (a) Before line 277 add qv = Q_0((z[:-1], (x.reshape(-1,1)*np.ones_like(z))[:-1], debt[:-1])) and df['debt_val'] = np.reshape(book[:-1,:].T*qv.T, (N*T,)); then replace line 278 with df['mkt_lev'] = df.debt_val/(df.debt_val + df.mve). (b) Keep book_lev (already built at line 243) as a char instead of dropping it. (c) Add df['dd'] = (z[:-1] - z_cut_down((xfull[:-1], debt[:-1])))/sqrt(GS21_SIGMA_Z**2/(1-GS21_RHO_Z**2)). (d) Add df['ivest'] = df.groupby('firmid').agr.rolling(12).mean(). (e) Add df['cfvol'] = df.groupby('firmid').roe.rolling(36, min_periods=24).std(). Q_0 and z_cut_down are already in scope: line 15 does from .sdf_compute_gs21 import *. config.py: line 223 CHARS_GS21 = ['size','bm','agr','roe','mom','mkt_lev','book_lev','dd','ivest','cfvol']; line 224 FACTOR_NAMES_GS21 extended to the same length. utils_factors/fama_functions.py: extend _CHAR_TO_FACTOR at line 63 and line 170 with the four new names -- fama_french builds name_dct at line 65 with an 'if c in' filter but indexes it unconditionally in the loop at line 67, so an unmapped char raises KeyError. Also extend config.py CHAR_TO_FACTOR near line 229. No re-solve, no change to sdf_compute.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: No new economic parameters; the only choices are the rolling windows. cfvol window = 36 months: the standard idiosyncratic-volatility estimation window, giving the proxy sampling noise of sigma/sqrt(2*36) = 11.8% of the true sigma, close to the noise-to-signal in real accounting-based cash-flow-volatility measures. ivest window = 12 months: the investment rate is 1.75%/month, so a 12-month window yields a Binomial(12, 0.0175) count with 12 distinct support points instead of agr's 2, and an expected annual capital growth of 12*0.0175*0.14 = 2.9%/yr, matching the model's own drift. dd is normalized by the stationary sd of z, sqrt(sigma_z^2/(1-rho_z^2)) = 0.0539 at current parameters. Caveat: with the current solfiles z_cut_down is pinned at the zgrid floor (-0.146826) at every (x,b), so dd is an affine transform of z and adds nothing until proposal 5 makes the default boundary interior. Ship it anyway -- it costs nothing and becomes the key char afterwards.
proposals.predicted_effect: In isolation: DKKM Sharpe +1% to +2% (0.511 -> ~0.52); FM Sharpe +1% to +3% (four more linear regressors, and its pinvh conditioning improves because mkt_lev is no longer three orders of magnitude smaller than size); FF roughly unchanged or slightly worse (four more sorts add estimation noise). The DKKM/FM gap may even NARROW slightly. HJD and max_sr essentially unchanged -- max_sr is a property of the model, not of the char set, and stays ~0.44/month. The value is entirely conditional: this is what lets proposals 1, 4 and 5 be represented at all, and it roughly doubles the RFF effective rank (measured 20.7 -> 38.5), the quantity DKKM's own theory says governs whether complexity pays.
risks: Adding characteristics is symmetric: FM gets them linearly too. If the truth stays near-linear this REDUCES the DKKM/FM gap, because DKKM pays estimation cost over a larger feature space while FM simply becomes better specified. Do not ship this alone as the fix.
dd is dead on arrival with the current solfiles (z_cut pinned at the grid floor everywhere), so it is a constant-plus-z column duplicating roe. Consider gating it on proposal 5.

cfvol requires 36 months of history, which interacts with the default-reset logic (default_lag at lines 257-263): firms with fewer than 24 months since reset are NaN and get dropped by prepare_panel. Inert today with zero defaults, but a real and SELECTIVE universe-shrinkage problem under proposal 5.

Each added char adds a column to the FF/FM OLS MVE (K = 7 -> 11), raising their plug-in Sharpe loss from roughly 2K/T = 3.9% to 6.1%. That is a small MECHANICAL handicap to the linear methods that a referee could object to; report the linear methods at both char sets.
proposals.implementation_cost: Zero cost in sdf_compute_gs21.py -- the conditional second moment is untouched, still O(N^2 n_x) per month and still exact. No MATLAB re-solve. The only runtime cost is in create_panel: one extra 3-D interpolator evaluation (Q_0) and one 2-D evaluation (z_cut_down) over the whole (T+1) x N panel, which is the same order as the interpolator work already done in create_arrays, plus two pandas rolling operations. Roughly 20 lines of new code across panel_functions_gs21.py, config.py and fama_functions.py. This is the cheapest item in the list by a wide margin.

proposals.name: Restore the idiosyncratic shock to the paper calibration, raise its persistence, and repair the four solve-vs-simulation parameter mismatches
proposals.one_line: The solfiles were solved with sigma_z = 0.00956 and sigma_x = 0.00707 while config.py simulates 1.468x and 1.484x those values (config uses rho^(3/2) where GS21.m uses rho^(2/3)); restore sigma_z to the paper's 0.0956 and raise rho_z from 0.9655 to 0.985, which is the only lever that makes the cross-section of book-to-market and idiosyncratic volatility remotely real.
proposals.economic_story: GS21's cross-section is degenerate because own productivity barely moves firm value. I measured d log P/d z = 0.18-0.21 at (b=0, x=0) against d log P/d x = 12.4 -- a 60:1 asymmetry. The reason is duration: equity is a ~170-month-duration claim, x has monthly persistence 0.983 (duration 59 months) while z has 0.9655 (duration 29 months), so z's innovations are largely averaged away before they matter. Combined with sigma_z having been cut 10x (commits eee2386 and dc2462e, 2026-06-09), the result is sd(log bm) = sd(log P_ex) = 0.101 against ~0.8 in CRSP, average pairwise return correlation 0.95-0.975 against ~0.17, and idiosyncratic/systematic volatility of 0.17 against ~2.2. The defensible fix is not just to undo the 10x cut but to fix the persistence: firm-level TFP and profitability are far more persistent than rho_z = 0.9^(1/3) implies. Foster-Haltiwanger-Syverson put annual plant-level TFP persistence at ~0.8; Fama-French (2000) put annual profitability persistence at ~0.85. Those correspond to monthly rho_z of 0.9816 and 0.9866. GS21's rho_z = 0.9655 corresponds to annual 0.667 -- far too transitory.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: This is the dispersion and signal-to-noise enabler and a precondition for every nonlinearity in the model to be reachable. Three channels. (i) It raises d log P/d z roughly in proportion to duration: from 0.29 (measured at b=0.3, x=0) to 0.29*(1/(1-0.985))/(1/(1-0.9655)) = 0.65, and raises the stationary sd of z from 0.0539 to 0.0956/sqrt(1-0.985^2) = 0.554. Together the z-driven component of sd(log P_ex) goes from 0.29*0.0539 = 0.016 to 0.65*0.554 = 0.36, a 23x increase in cross-sectional value dispersion; sd(log bm) goes from 0.101 to ~0.37 -- still below CRSP's ~0.8 but within a factor of 2 rather than 8. (ii) The elasticity d log P/d z is itself strongly state-dependent: I measured 0.18-0.21 at (b=0, x=0), 0.56-0.65 at (b=1, x=0), 0.69-0.86 at (b=1, x=-4sd) and 0.10-0.13 at (b=0, x=+4sd) -- an 8.6x range over the solved grid, generated by a leverage x aggregate-state INTERACTION. Today only the 0.20-0.35 sub-range is realized. Widening the realized (z, b, x) support turns idiosyncratic variance d_i into an interactive, convex function of (mkt_lev, roe, x_t) with an 8x range in volatility and 70x in variance, which is exactly the multiplier that turns a nonlinear alpha into a large DKKM edge. (iii) It fixes the SNR: with idio vol at 2.0%/month and a per-firm information ratio of 0.021, GS21's alpha leg is a synthetic near-arbitrage that scales as sqrt(N); raising idio vol 3-5x pushes it toward the regime where estimation costs something and shrinkage can pay.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: Standalone, FM captures MOST of it, and I want to be explicit about that. An inverse-variance tilt 1/d_i that is a monotone function of a single characteristic is nearly linear in rank space: I computed the linear R^2 of exp(-c u) for u ~ U[-0.5,0.5] to be 0.921 at a 10x range, 0.861 at 25x and 0.763 at 100x, with the quadratic R^2 at 0.997, 0.991 and 0.971. So a monotone heteroskedasticity channel hands FM 76-92% of itself. The DKKM-specific content here is the INTERACTION: d_i = f(book_lev_i, roe_i)*g(x_t) with f jointly convex, and I measured the two-characteristic multiplicative version at linear R^2 = 0.458 (100x range per char) versus 0.815 quadratic. So this proposal's honest standalone contribution to the DKKM/FM gap is modest; its real role is to raise the amplitude of proposals 1, 4 and 5 by an order of magnitude.
proposals.exact_change: config.py line 286: GS21_SIGMA_X = 0.012*np.sqrt((1 - 0.95**(3/2))/(1 - 0.95**2)) -> use (2/3) as in GS21.m line 23, giving 0.0070688. Line 289: GS21_SIGMA_Z = 0.1*0.16*np.sqrt((1 - 0.9**(3/2))/(1 - 0.9**2)) -> 0.16*np.sqrt((1 - 0.9**(2/3))/(1 - 0.9**2)) = 0.095599 (drop the 0.1 factor AND fix the exponent). Line 288: GS21_RHO_Z = 0.90**(1/3) -> 0.985. Line 299: GS21_R = 0.074830/12 = 0.0062358 disagrees with GS21.m line 27 r = 0.1/12 = 0.0083333 -- pick one and use it in both. utils_gs21/panel_functions_gs21.py lines 113-118 apply (1-tau) to operating profit while GS21.m line 127 does not (pi_Rmat = exp(x+z) - delta - (1-tau)*b) -- reconcile, since P_ex = P - Ecashflow (line 129) is otherwise internally inconsistent by tau*exp(x+z) ~ 0.067 out of ~190. GS21.m: line 24 rho_z, line 25 sigma_z, and line 50 znum 200 -> at least 400 (the grid must span +/-4*0.554 = +/-2.22 instead of +/-0.147, a 15x widening; keeping the current spacing would need ~3000 points). Full re-solve.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: sigma_z = 0.095599: exactly GS21.m line 25 as written (0.16*sqrt((1-0.9^(2/3))/(1-0.9^2))), i.e. the model's own documented calibration with the ad hoc 0.1 factor added on 2026-06-09 removed. rho_z = 0.985: the monthly equivalent of an annual AR(1) of 0.985^12 = 0.834, matching Foster-Haltiwanger-Syverson's ~0.8 annual plant-TFP persistence and sitting just below Fama-French's ~0.85 annual profitability persistence. Resulting stationary sd(z) = 0.095599/sqrt(1-0.985^2) = 0.095599/0.17255 = 0.554. Same verification for z: 4*0.036707 = 0.146826 = zgrid.max() exactly.

Average pairwise return correlation 0.95-0.975 -> 0.35-0.55 (real ~0.17); idio/systematic vol ratio 0.17 -> 0.6-0.9 (real ~2.2); sd(log bm) 0.101 -> ~0.37. Keeping 200 points means 15x coarser spacing, visibly degrading the interpolated P_up/P_down and the cutoffs; going to 3000 points multiplies statenum from 80,000 to 1,200,000 and Mmat from 2.56 GB to ~576 GB. Restoring sigma_z 10x re-opens the pathology the 2026-06-09 cut presumably suppressed: the prior diagnosis records true SDF weights up to 1e9 under the original-vol calibration, traced to the arbitrary P_ex floor at panel_functions_gs21.py line 131 (P_ex = np.maximum(0.05/k, P_ex)) producing near-singular cond_var that scipy.linalg.solve accepts silently. That floor must be removed or replaced with a proper default before this is safe.

Lowering sigma_x 1.484x to match the solve reduces aggregate volatility and hence the level of every Sharpe. If you prefer the higher sigma_x, re-solve with a wider x grid instead -- but do not leave the mismatch in place, because the current run extrapolates the solved value function outside its grid.
This changes the model's headline moments enough that the paper's GS21 calibration section must be rewritten and re-defended. A paper cost, not a code cost, but real.
proposals.implementation_cost: sdf_compute_gs21.py needs only the new sigma_z/rho_z constants -- the quadrature at lines 91-92 already uses them and the O(N^2 n_x) structure is untouched, so the conditional second moment remains exactly computable at unchanged cost. The entire burden is the MATLAB re-solve, and it is the memory-bound one: the dense Mmat construction at GS21.m lines 138-139 is statenum x (xnum*znum) and does not survive a 15x wider z grid at the current 200 points, let alone 3000. Either reduce znum and accept coarser resolution, or rewrite the VFI to use sparse transitions. Also note the interpolators' fill_value=None (sdf_compute_gs21.py lines 61-74) silently linearly extrapolates off-grid, which is how the current 1.48x mismatch has gone unnoticed -- add an explicit off-grid counter to the simulation as a guard.

proposals.name: Permanent cross-sectional heterogeneity in asset risk: J discrete industry types with different sigma_z
proposals.one_line: Give firms one of five permanent cash-flow-volatility types spanning a 5x range, so idiosyncratic return variance spans ~25x, optimal leverage differs by type, and the type is observable to the econometrician only through a noisy 36-month rolling cash-flow-volatility proxy.
proposals.economic_story: GS21 assumes a single sigma_z for every firm, so all firms have identical asset risk. This is the least defensible homogeneity assumption in the model: industry cash-flow volatility differs by roughly an order of magnitude (utilities and staples versus biotech and semiconductors), and it is the primary determinant of both optimal leverage (the standard tradeoff prediction, confirmed since Titman-Wessels) and idiosyncratic equity volatility. Ang-Hodrick-Xing-Zhang's idiosyncratic-volatility quintiles average roughly 3.3%/month and 16%/month, a 4.8x range, which the current GS21 replicates as 1.54% to 2.67%, a 1.7x range. Adding permanent type heterogeneity introduces no new economics -- only a re-solve per type.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: The true MVE weight in GS21 is exactly w* = D^{-1}(mu - beta*lambda) -- the prior diagnosis verified corr(w*, alpha_i/idio_var_i) = -1.000 at three separate dates, so the inverse-idiosyncratic-variance tilt IS the true weight. This proposal attacks D directly. With sigma_{z,i} spanning 5x, d_i spans 25x from the type channel alone, multiplied by the 8.6x elasticity range that proposal 3 unlocks, for a total idiosyncratic-variance range above 100x (real-data-like). Three DKKM-specific consequences. (i) The type is observable only through a noisy proxy: a 36-month rolling volatility estimate has sampling sd sigma/sqrt(2*36) = 11.8% of sigma, so the econometrician's char is the state plus noise -- the DKKM/AIPT theory needs exactly this and GS21 currently has zero measurement error in every char. (ii) Optimal leverage b*(sigma_{z,j}) is DECREASING in type volatility, so the same observed book_lev means very different distress risk across types: the relevant object is the RATIO book_lev_i / b*(cfvol_i), not a linear combination. (iii) It multiplies proposal 1: the V-shape |b_i - b*(z_i, x_t, sigma_{z,j})| acquires a type-dependent vertex, so the object DKKM must fit becomes |mkt_lev - h(roe, size, cfvol)| -- a moving-vertex kink in a three-characteristic index.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: Partly they can, and I want to be explicit about the part they can. A monotone inverse-variance tilt in one characteristic is nearly linear in rank space: I computed the linear R^2 of exp(-c u) at 0.861 for a 25x range and 0.763 for 100x, with quadratic R^2 of 0.991 and 0.971. So FM harvests 76-86% of the pure heteroskedasticity channel -- which is exactly why the prior diagnosis found GS21's entire quadratic headroom worth only 0.871 -> 0.909 of max SR^2. The parts FM and FF structurally cannot get are: (a) the RATIO book_lev/b*(cfvol) -- FM is linear in book_lev and linear in cfvol, and I measured a two-characteristic multiplicative object at linear R^2 = 0.458 (100x range per char) versus 0.815 quadratic; (b) the type-dependent vertex of proposal 1's V -- a symmetric function has exactly zero linear projection (verified R^2 = 0.000) and a 2x3 sort on any single char nets it to zero; (c) the optimal weight is E[1/sigma_z | cfvol_observed], a nonlinear SHRINKAGE map of a noisy proxy, and FM's unpenalized OLS on cfvol (ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0], config.py line 187) cannot represent a shrinkage map. Point (c) is the cleanest formal argument.
proposals.exact_change: GS21.m: wrap the whole VFI (lines 172-371) in for j = 1:5 with sigma_z = sigma_z_bar*mult(j) at line 25 and a per-type tauchen call at line 74; write outputs to GS21_solfiles/type<j>/. Grid dimensions and per-type cost unchanged; total cost is 5x one solve. utils_gs21/sdf_compute_gs21.py lines 27-74: convert the module-level grid reads and interpolator constructions into a list indexed by type, SOL[j] = dict(P_up=..., P_down=..., ...). utils_gs21/panel_functions_gs21.py: add ftype = np.random.randint(0,5,N) in create_arrays and dispatch every interpolator call (lines 68-69, 94, 98-99, 116-118, 190-197) by type -- the clean implementation evaluates all five interpolators on the full cross-section and selects with np.choose (5x interpolation time, no extra memory); line 42 must use sigma_z[ftype] in simulate_ar1 and lines 80/84 must re-draw the type on default replacement. utils_gs21/sdf_compute_gs21.py line 91: zi = rho_z*zi_prev + sigma_z*np.tile(nodes,n) becomes sigma_z_vec[:,None]*np.tile(nodes,n) -- one line, already broadcast-shaped since zi_prev is N x 1. Lines 121-128 and 173-184 need the same per-firm np.choose dispatch. config.py: add GS21_SIGMA_Z_MULT = [0.447, 0.719, 1.0, 1.391, 2.238].
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: J = 5 permanent types, sigma_{z,j} = sigmabar_z*exp(kappa*q_j) with q_j the quintile midpoints of a standard normal, q = {-1.282, -0.524, 0, +0.524, +1.282}. Set the 10th-to-90th ratio to 5.0: exp(kappa*(1.282-(-1.282))) = 5 => kappa = ln(5)/2.564 = 0.6277, giving multipliers {0.447, 0.719, 1.000, 1.391, 2.238}. Target justification: Ang-Hodrick-Xing-Zhang idiosyncratic-volatility quintile portfolios span roughly 3.3%/month to 16%/month (4.8x in volatility), and Compustat quarterly sales-growth and cash-flow volatility have a 10-90 range of roughly 4-6x across firms. So 5.0x in sigma_z, hence 25x in variance, is the right target. sigmabar_z = 0.095599 from proposal 3. Types drawn once at firm birth (and re-drawn on default replacement) with probability 1/5 each. cfvol proxy window = 36 months (proposal 2). Predicted realized idio-volatility range: 5x from the type channel times 2-3x from the leverage/state elasticity channel = 10-15x, versus ~4.8x in AHXZ -- if it comes out too wide, cut kappa to ln(3.5)/2.564 = 0.489.
proposals.predicted_effect: Standalone: idio-volatility cross-sectional range 1.7x -> ~5x, sd(log idio variance) from ~0.25 to ~0.75. Population linear-6 span falls from 0.871 to roughly 0.75-0.82 of max SR^2 (most of the new content is monotone), RFF360 stays at 0.97-0.99, so population DKKM/FM in Sharpe goes from ~1.03 to ~1.10-1.15. Realized: DKKM +5-10%, FM +2-5%, FF flat or down (value weighting kills the high-idio-vol tail). Standalone this is a small win. As a MULTIPLIER on proposal 1: the prior oracle-span experiment found that adding characteristic-linked heteroskedastic D raised the RFF-over-linear ceiling from 2.88x to 6.37x with a nonlinear alpha and from 1.00x to 1.91x with a linear alpha. Applying that logic, proposal 1's expected ~1.8x population gap should go to ~2.5-3.0x with this proposal -- the first combination in this list that plausibly reaches real-data magnitudes. HJD should separate cleanly for the first time, because the alpha/d ratio DKKM can represent and FM cannot now carries most of SR^2.
risks: If the type is too easily inferred from cfvol, FM recovers most of the gain -- the whole DKKM edge here rests on the proxy being NOISY and the optimal map being a nonlinear shrinkage. Verify by regressing the true 1/sigma_{z,i} on the rank of cfvol_i linearly and nonlinearly; if the linear R^2 exceeds ~0.85 the channel is inert and either kappa or the window must change (shorten to 24 months to raise the proxy noise to 14.4%).

b*(sigma_{z,j}) may not differ much across types, because in this calibration the debt tradeoff is dominated by the tax shield and default never happens; if b* comes out nearly identical for all five types then the ratio channel evaporates and only the D^{-1} channel survives. Check the re-solved b_refin_0 files first.
Five sets of solfiles is ~80 MB of CSVs, and the module-level read at sdf_compute_gs21.py lines 37-50 happens at import time -- it will become slow and memory-heavy. Convert to .npz and lazy-load.

Permanent never-changing types make part of the cross-sectional structure a fixed effect, which the 360-month rolling window can learn almost perfectly -- that HELPS the linear methods. Consider a slow Markov industry-migration process instead of strictly permanent types.

Type heterogeneity in sigma_z means the z quadrature nodes differ across firms, which is fine for the second moment (z is integrated out per firm) but means the panel's z process is no longer a single AR(1); any downstream code assuming a common sigma_z (e.g. the dd normalization in proposal 2) must be made type-aware.
proposals.implementation_cost: The conditional second moment REMAINS exactly computable and the O(N^2 n_x) structure is preserved, because sigma_z only enters the FIRM-SPECIFIC z' quadrature at sdf_compute_gs21.py line 91, which is integrated out per firm at lines 135-136 BEFORE the outer product over the shared x' nodes at line 141. That two-stage separation is exactly what makes type heterogeneity free at the N^2 level. The cost is a 5x increase in the interpolator evaluation count in both create_arrays and integ_zi_zj_x (the N x n^2 = 1000 x 100 = 100,000-point evaluations per interpolator per month go to 5x if implemented with np.choose over all five types; grouping firms by type and slicing avoids the 5x at the price of more code). Five MATLAB re-solves at unchanged grid dimensions, each identical in cost to the current one. Roughly 60-80 lines of restructuring across sdf_compute_gs21.py and panel_functions_gs21.py, mostly mechanical dispatch.

proposals.name: HIGH RISK / HIGH REWARD: turn on the equity-issuance kink kappa_e and widen the debt grid so both the negative-cash-flow region and the default boundary are actually reachable
proposals.one_line: GS21.m already contains a kink at zero cash flow -- (1 + (prof<=0)*kappa_e)*prof at lines 253-254 and 259-260 -- but kappa_e is 0 and the region is unreachable because the maximum coupon is 1 against gross profit of ~1; raise kappa_e to 0.05, tau to 0.20 and bmax to 1.5-2, and simulate the sigma_m valuation shock the solver already assumes.
proposals.economic_story: GS21's whole point is that financial frictions price the cross-section, and the model contains three: proportional equity-issuance costs kappa_e, proportional debt-issuance costs kappa_b, and endogenous default. In the shipped calibration kappa_e = 0 (config.py line 294; GS21.m line 33 shows the intended 0.025 commented out), kappa_b = 0.004 is an order of magnitude below observed underwriting spreads, and default has probability zero: I verified that the global minimum of the solved value function over the ENTIRE 200x20x20 grid, including b = 1 and z, x at -4 standard deviations, is P_down = 4.73 > 0, that z_cut_down is pinned at the zgrid floor at every (x,b), and that the simulated minimum equity price is 30.4. Separately, the MATLAB solver assumes an i.i.d. valuation shock nu ~ N(0, sigma_m^2 = 25) added to P inside the default indicator (GS21.m lines 53-59, 204, 210, 263-264), and the Python simulation never draws it (panel_functions_gs21.py line 72 tests P <= 0 with no shock) -- so the simulation is not even internally consistent with the solve. Turning on frictions the model already contains is the least ad hoc way to give GS21 a genuine nonlinearity.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: Two kinks, both located in characteristic space. (1) The equity-issuance kink: operating profit is prof_it = exp(x_t + z_it) - delta - (1-tau)*b_it and P is a KINKED function of prof at prof = 0, with left slope (1+kappa_e) and right slope 1. The kink is a THRESHOLD in the joint (roe, book_lev) plane whose intercept moves with x_t: firms cross when exp(x+z) <= delta + (1-tau)b. The x-exposure jumps discretely at the boundary, so beta_x,i has a step in a two-characteristic index. (2) Default: once P can reach zero, d log P/d z explodes as option leverage. I measured it already varying 8.6x over the solved grid (0.10 at b=0, x=+4sd up to 0.86 at b=1, x=-4sd), and it diverges as P -> 0. Idiosyncratic variance becomes a convex, near-exponential function of distance-to-default with a range of 100x or more; the default JUMP itself carries a priced, characteristic-dependent intensity; and the model's own z_cut interpolators (shipped, unused) give a clean distance-to-default characteristic. This is the one channel in GS21 that can plausibly deliver the real-data 100x dispersion in idiosyncratic volatility and the fat left tail of small distressed names that DKKM's own decomposition shows carries most of their Sharpe (their mega/large-cap-only Sharpe is 1.6 against 3.7 full sample).
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: The default-probability channel is convex but MONOTONE in distance-to-default, so if distance-to-default is supplied as a characteristic (proposal 2) FM gets a lot of it -- I measured the linear R^2 of exp(-c u) at 0.763 even for a 100x range. The DKKM edge is therefore NOT the convexity. It is three specific things. (a) A step in the TAIL of a characteristic is far less linear than a step at the median: for u ~ U[-0.5,0.5] the linear R^2 of 1{u > median} is 0.75, but of 1{u > 10th percentile} it is only 0.27. Both the kappa_e kink and the default boundary bind in the left tail of the (roe, book_lev) index, so a linear projection captures roughly a quarter of them. (b) FF's 2x3 sorts value-weight, so the distressed left tail -- which is exactly where the kinks are and which is by construction the small-cap end -- receives near-zero weight in every FF factor. FM has no such problem but is linear. (c) The kink LOCATION depends on the aggregate state x_t, so the correct weight is 1{roe_i < a(x_t) + b*book_lev_i}: FM is re-estimated monthly so it can shift an intercept, but it cannot bend, and a step whose location moves is still a step.
proposals.exact_change: config.py line 294: GS21_KAPPA_E = 0 -> 0.05; line 292 GS21_TAU = 0.2/3 -> 0.20; add GS21_SIGMA_M. GS21.m: line 33 kappa_e -> 0.05, line 31 tau -> 0.20, line 42 bmax 1 -> 1.5 (or 2), line 43 bnum 20 -> 30, line 50 znum 200 -> 100 to keep the dense Mmat (statenum x xnum*znum) at 30*20*100 x 20*100 = 60,000 x 2,000 = 0.96 GB instead of 2.56 GB. Nothing else changes in GS21.m: the kappa_e code path at lines 253-254 and 259-260 and the sigma_m default smoothing at lines 55-59, 204, 210, 263-264 are ALREADY WRITTEN and merely inert at kappa_e = 0 and the current leverage scale. utils_gs21/panel_functions_gs21.py: line 72 default[t] = (P[t] <= 0) -> draw nu ~ N(0, GS21_SIGMA_M^2) truncated to |nu| < 4*sigma_m (matching GS21.m line 54's mbar = 4*sigma_m) and test P[t] + nu <= 0; the replacement machinery at lines 73-89 then works unchanged, but the while loop at line 73 needs an iteration cap and line 85's failure to write the redrawn xt back into x[t] must be fixed. Line 131's arbitrary floor P_ex = np.maximum(0.05/k, P_ex) must be removed once default is real. utils_gs21/sdf_compute_gs21.py: the conditional second moment must add the default branch -- payoff becomes (1 - pdef)*P' for the cross term and the same with the squared payoff on the diagonal, with pdef = Phi(-P'(z',x',b')/sigma_m) evaluated pointwise at every quadrature node. Four to six lines, and it does NOT change the O(N^2 n_x) structure because default is conditionally independent across firms given (x', z_i').
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: kappa_e = 0.05: Hennessy and Whited (2007) estimate the linear component of equity flotation costs at ~5.0% of proceeds for the median firm (8-9% for small firms); GS21.m's own commented value is 0.025, so 0.05 is at the upper end of what the authors already contemplated. tau = 0.20 (see proposal 1: a marginal tax rate must not be divided by 3, and the resulting capitalized shield of 5.9% of equity value moves toward Graham's 9.7%). bmax = 1.5-2: the binding target is interest coverage. b is the monthly coupon per unit capital and gross profit is exp(x+z) ~ 1 per unit capital per month, so b IS the inverse interest-coverage ratio. Current bmax = 1 means coverage 1.0 is the worst state the grid allows; US high-yield issuers routinely run EBIT/interest below 1.0 and distressed issuers below 0.5, so bmax = 1.5 (coverage 0.67) is the minimum for a live default region and bmax = 2 (coverage 0.5) is safer. Verify after re-solving that P_down at (z_min, x_min, bmax) is negative -- it is currently 4.73 at bmax = 1 (I measured 11.73, 7.48, 4.73 at b = 0.3, 0.6, 1.0). sigma_m: target an unconditional default rate of 1.0%/year (Moody's all-corporate 1970-2020 average ~1.5%/yr; investment grade 0.1%, speculative grade 4%). Since the default probability is E[Phi(-P/sigma_m)], sigma_m must be chosen by a one-dimensional search on a simulated panel AFTER the re-solve. With the current P distribution (mean 190, min 165) even sigma_m = 60 gives Phi(-3.17) = 0.08%/month = 0.9%/yr, so sigma_m must be recalibrated jointly with bmax and sigma_z -- do NOT ship sigma_m = 5 against the current P scale, it is exactly zero. Internal consistency requirement: whatever sigma_m the simulation draws must be the sigma_m the MATLAB solve used.
proposals.predicted_effect: If it works: idiosyncratic-volatility cross-sectional range from 1.7x to 20-100x, sd(log idio variance) from ~0.25 to ~1.0-1.3 (real-data levels), a genuine fat left tail, and a finally non-degenerate distance-to-default characteristic. Population linear-6 span should fall to 0.35-0.55 of max SR^2 with RFF360 holding 0.85-0.95, giving a population DKKM/FM Sharpe ratio of 1.3-1.6x from this proposal alone and 2.5-4x combined with proposals 1 and 4. FF should degrade badly and visibly, because value weighting excludes exactly the distressed names carrying the premium -- a DKKM/FF gap of 2-3x is plausible, which is the number the paper needs. max_sr should rise, and HJD should finally separate because the true HJ portfolio will load heavily on a distressed tail FF cannot touch. If it does not work, nothing changes at all, because the kinks stay unreachable.
risks: Highest probability of no effect. All three sub-changes are currently inert for the same reason: the state never gets near the kink. tau = 0.20 raises b*, but if b* lands at 0.5 then prof = 1 - 0.0067 - 0.4 = +0.59 and the kappa_e kink still needs exp(x+z) <= 0.407, i.e. -0.9 in logs, which is -2.4 sd even with proposal 3's restored sigma_z. This proposal is CONDITIONAL on proposal 3 and probably on bmax = 2 rather than 1.5. Check reachability on the re-solved grid before running anything else.

Re-opens the 1e9 SDF-weight pathology. The prior diagnosis traced it to panel_functions_gs21.py line 131's P_ex floor producing near-singular cond_var that scipy.linalg.solve(..., assume_a='pos') accepts silently -- note sdf_compute_gs21.py line 207 also calls scipy.linalg without importing it, which resolves only by accident. With real defaults, prices genuinely approach zero and returns approach -100%, so ER conditioning will degrade for real. Add an explicit minimum-eigenvalue check and exclude sub-floor firms from the ER solve, exactly as the KP14 book>0 fix does.

The default-replacement machinery at panel_functions_gs21.py lines 73-89 has two latent bugs that only fire once defaults exist: the all-firms-default branch redraws xt without writing it back into x[t] (line 85), leaving the returned x path inconsistent with prices and with the sdf_compute call at line 197, and the enclosing while loop has no iteration cap and can spin forever if replacements also default. Fix both first.

A live default rate breaks panel balance: firms reset with k = 0.2*mean(k) and b = 0, roe and mom become NaN for 12 months (lines 275, 285), and prepare_panel drops them. At 1%/yr that is ~1% of firm-months, tolerable; at 5%/yr it materially and SELECTIVELY shrinks the sample on exactly the distressed firms carrying the premium, which would bias every method including DKKM.

This is the largest re-solve in the list (kappa_e changes the fixed point, tau changes optimal leverage, bmax changes the grid) and the tauchen dependency is still missing. Budget a Python port of GS21.m.
proposals.implementation_cost: sdf_compute_gs21.py stays O(N^2 n_x) and the conditional second moment stays exactly computable: default is conditionally independent across firms given (x', z_i'), so the survival probability (1 - Phi(-P'/sigma_m)) multiplies each firm's payoff BEFORE the two-stage integration (integrate z_i' out at lines 135-136, then outer-product over shared x' at line 141). Four to six lines, plus the same treatment in the diagonal at lines 173-184 (where the second moment of a Bernoulli-mixed payoff is (1-pdef)*P'^2, not ((1-pdef)*P')^2 -- get this right or the diagonal will be biased downward). One extra normal-CDF evaluation per quadrature node, negligible. The real costs are the MATLAB re-solve (which must also reduce znum to keep Mmat under a few GB after bnum increases) and the joint calibration search over (bmax, sigma_m) to hit a 1%/yr default rate, which requires iterating solve-then-simulate two or three times.

proposals.name: A genuinely independent second priced aggregate shock: a credit-conditions state s_t with its own price of risk
proposals.one_line: Promote proposal 1's zeta from a function of x to an independent AR(1) state s_t with its own price of risk gamma_s in the SDF, so GS21 has TWO priced aggregate shocks with orthogonal, differently-shaped cross-sectional loadings -- the only change in this list that raises the dimension of the priced-risk space.
proposals.economic_story: Every diagnosis of all three models converges on the same point: with one priced aggregate shock, expected returns are rank-one in the covariance loadings and there is no dimension for complexity to explore. GS21's natural second shock is a credit-supply / intermediary shock: the availability and price of external finance moves independently of productivity (He-Krishnamurthy's intermediary capital factor, Gilchrist-Zakrajsek's excess bond premium, and the 2008 and 2020 episodes are the canonical cases where credit conditions moved without a contemporaneous TFP shock). Because GS21 already has an explicit external-finance friction -- the Poisson refinancing opportunity plus proportional issuance costs -- a credit-conditions state is not a bolt-on; it is the natural stochastic version of a parameter the model already has. It is priced because intermediary capital is a documented priced factor with an annual Sharpe of roughly 0.3-0.4.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: With two priced shocks the true expected return is mu_i = beta_x,i*lambda_x + beta_s,i*lambda_s, and the two loadings have completely different shapes in characteristic space. I measured beta_x to be essentially FLAT in leverage: d log P/d x is 27.3 at b=0 versus 24.0 at b=1 at x = -4sd, and 7.5 versus 8.5 at x = +4sd -- there is no financial-leverage amplification of the aggregate beta in this model, because debt value is as x-elastic as equity value. beta_s, by contrast, is proportional to (P_up - P_down)/P_ex, which is zero at the target capital structure and symmetrically positive on both sides. So the two loadings are orthogonal in shape: one is a near-constant, the other a symmetric V in a characteristic index. This is DKKM's condition (C3): priced directions that are quasi-orthogonal and spread across the spectrum rather than concentrated in one eigenvector. It also raises the priced rank of the conditional covariance from the measured 1 (top eigenvalue 97.34% of total variance, the remaining spectrum entirely the idiosyncratic bulk) to 2, with a second factor carrying a non-trivial share. Proposal 1 gives the nonlinear LOADING; only this proposal gives the second SHOCK, and hence the second priced direction that a rank-two mu requires.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: The same formal argument as proposal 1, strengthened. The additional premium component is beta_s,i*lambda_s with beta_s,i = (P_up_i - P_down_i)/P_ex,i, a symmetric quadratic in (book_lev_i - b*(roe_i, size_i, s_t)). A symmetric function of a characteristic has exactly zero covariance with that characteristic (I verified linear R^2 = 0.000 for exp(-c|u|) at every amplitude), so FM's X(X'X)^{-1} weights place exactly zero loading on it, and FF's 2x3 high-minus-low sort on book_lev nets the two extreme terciles against each other and also gets ~zero. Beyond that, the linear methods now cannot HEDGE the second factor either -- w* = D^{-1}(mu - B c) requires a portfolio orthogonal to beta_s, which is unreachable inside the linear-char span -- so they lose twice: they forgo lambda_s and they carry unhedged s-risk. DKKM's cos-half features are literally rank(-|w'x|) after the second rank-standardization, which is the correct functional form.
proposals.exact_change: GS21.m: add s as a fourth state. Discretize with tauchen (rho_s, sigma_s, snum = 5) and set statenum = bnum*xnum*znum*snum. Set zeta_s = zetabar*exp(theta_s*s). Line 138's SDF becomes Mmat = exp(-r - 0.5*gamma_x^2 - 0.5*gamma_s^2 - gamma_x*eps_x' - gamma_s*eps_s') with eps_s' = (s' - (1-rho_s)*sbar - rho_s*s)/sigma_s. Substitute zeta_s for the scalar xi at lines 216, 273, 280. CRITICAL: the current implementation forms dense statenum x (xnum*znum) matrices (Mmat at line 139 is already 80,000 x 4,000 = 2.56 GB); with snum = 5 this becomes 400,000 x 20,000 = 64 GB and is infeasible. The VFI must be rewritten to use the sparse Kronecker transition (pr_mat is already built with kron at lines 75-76) and to loop over the s dimension, or znum must be cut hard. Budget this as a genuine rewrite of GS21.m, not an edit. utils_gs21/sdf_compute_gs21.py: all interpolators at lines 61-74 become 4-dimensional in (z, x, b, s), and integ_zi_zj_x gets a third quadrature dimension. The critical structural property SURVIVES: s' is a SHARED node like x', so the two-stage pattern -- integrate the firm-specific z_i' out at lines 135-136 to an N x (n_x*n_s) matrix, then outer-product over the shared nodes at line 141 -- still yields the exact N x N second moment, at cost O(N^2 n_x n_s). That is about 10 lines. utils_gs21/panel_functions_gs21.py: simulate s alongside x in simulate_ar1 (lines 21-44) and thread it through every interpolator call and through integ_zi_x.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: rho_s = 0.95^(1/3) = 0.98305, matching x's persistence (credit conditions are about as persistent as the business cycle; the excess bond premium has a monthly AR(1) of roughly 0.93-0.96, so use 0.95 if you prefer the EBP estimate directly). theta_s calibrated so a one-standard-deviation move in s changes the refinancing intensity by the same amount proposal 1's theta_zeta = 0.46 delivers for x; normalizing sd(s) = 1 gives theta_s = 0.46. gamma_s: target an annualized Sharpe of 0.35 on the credit factor, matching He-Kelly-Manela's intermediary capital risk factor (annual Sharpe ~0.35-0.45) and Gilchrist-Zakrajsek's EBP-mimicking portfolio. Monthly gamma_s = 0.35/sqrt(12) = 0.101, versus gamma_x = 0.5 monthly (GS21.m line 28, a monthly Sharpe of 0.53) -- so the credit shock carries about one fifth of the x shock's price of risk. That ratio sets the fraction of SR^2 living in the nonlinear direction. Because the nonlinear loading also has a far larger cross-sectional DISPERSION (all of beta_s versus 3.7% of beta_x), the credit factor should carry the majority of the CROSS-SECTIONAL premium even at one fifth of the price of risk. Arithmetic: cross-sectional sd of the premium from x is sd(beta_x)*lambda_x = 0.00133*0.5 = 6.7e-4; from s it is sd(G/P)*theta_s*gamma_s. At the CURRENT sd(G/P) = 0.00241 that is 1.1e-4, only 17% -- so this proposal MUST be combined with proposal 1's tau and kappa_b recalibration (targeting sd(G/P) ~ 0.007, giving 3.3e-4, or 33% of the total, all non-monotone). To push the non-monotone share above 80% you need sd(G/P) ~ 0.03, i.e. the refinancing option worth 3% of equity value, which requires proposals 3 and 5 as well.
proposals.predicted_effect: The only proposal here that changes GS21's structural identity from a one-factor to a two-factor economy, so the only one that answers the 'GS21 has one shock' objection directly. Systematic rank of the conditional covariance 1 -> 2, with the second eigenvalue at maybe 5-20% of the first versus the current 0.03%. With the full package (this plus proposals 1, 3, 4) I would expect the population linear-6 span at 0.10-0.25 of max SR^2 and RFF360 at 0.80-0.92, i.e. a population DKKM/FM Sharpe ratio of 2.0-3.0x and DKKM/FF of 2.5-4x -- real-data magnitudes. RFF effective rank should rise materially because the priced directions are now spread over two quasi-orthogonal shapes. Alone, without the amplitude recalibration, expect only ~1.2-1.3x, because sd(G/P) = 0.0024 makes the second factor economically trivial. max_sr rises by roughly sqrt(1 + (lambda_s/lambda_x)^2) = 1.02 from the aggregate channel plus considerably more from the new cross-sectional dispersion.
risks: The MATLAB memory wall is hard: Mmat at snum = 5 is 64 GB dense. There is no way to do this without rewriting the VFI to exploit the Kronecker structure or shrinking znum from 200 to ~60. This is the dominant cost and it is not small.

tauchen.m is missing from the repo and no MATLAB or Octave is installed on this machine, so the re-solve pipeline does not currently exist at all. This proposal presupposes MATLAB plus tauchen, or a Python port of GS21.m (~200 lines, which I would recommend anyway).

The GS21 paper has no credit-supply shock. Adding one changes the model's identity more than any other proposal here, and a referee could reasonably say it is no longer Gomes-Schmid. Frame it as stochastic external-finance conditions in a model whose defining friction IS external finance, and cite He-Krishnamurthy and Gilchrist-Zakrajsek.

gamma_s is a free parameter disciplined only by a target Sharpe. That is the same status as gamma_x = 0.5 in GS21.m -- also free, also uncalibrated to anything in the firm problem. Note too that the declared Epstein-Zin parameters at GS21.m lines 14-16 (beta, varphi = 2, gamma = 10) are NEVER USED: the SDF is an exogenous lognormal with a constant price of risk. Be explicit in the paper rather than implying the SDF is derived from preferences.

If s ends up nearly perfectly correlated with x in the calibration, you have bought nothing over proposal 1 at 20x the cost. Keep corr(eps_s, eps_x) = 0 in the baseline and report the correlated case only as a robustness check.
proposals.implementation_cost: The conditional second moment REMAINS exactly computable, and this is the key implementation fact: s' is a shared aggregate node exactly like x', so the existing two-stage pattern in integ_zi_zj_x survives verbatim -- integrate the firm-specific z_i' out at lines 135-136 to get an N x (n_x*n_s) matrix, then form the outer product over the shared (x', s') nodes at line 141. Cost goes from O(N^2 n_x) to O(N^2 n_x n_s); with n_s = 3-5 Gauss-Hermite nodes (ample for a slow-moving state) that is a 3-5x increase, and the diagonal at lines 173-184 scales the same way. The interpolator evaluation count is the binding practical cost: N*n_z*n_x*n_s = 1000*10*10*5 = 500,000 points per interpolator per month, times eight interpolators, times 360 months -- keep n_s at 3 if this is too slow. All interpolators become 4-D RegularGridInterpolators, which is a mechanical change. The MATLAB side is the real cost: a rewrite of the VFI to avoid the 64 GB dense Mmat, plus a fourth grid dimension throughout, plus the missing tauchen. Treat this as the multi-week option and proposal 1 as its cheap 80%-of-the-benefit substitute.
